topic: MiniMax H3-Image in ComfyUI: local image gen today
thesis: MiniMax's H3-Image open-weight image model went from API-only to running in ComfyUI on your own GPU in three days, and tonight the whole thing is four files into three folders.
explanation_path: Start with what the viewer already does: typing a prompt into a chatbot and getting a picture back from somebody else's server. Establish what changed on 2026-11-08: MiniMax put the H3-Image weights on Hugging Face under a community license anyone can download. Before the how, land what the model is: one checkpoint that both generates from text and edits existing pictures, at about 16 megapixels natively (4096 x 4096), in 6 steps with no negative prompt -- because the numbers are the reason anyone cares. Then the practical machine-check moment: this is a 33.1B-parameter model whose full checkpoint is 68.65 GB and whose text encoder alone is 66.7 GB in BF16, which is why nobody runs it raw; the Comfy-Org INT8 repack is the version that fits a gaming PC, four files totalling about 54.79 GB. Only then walk the install: update ComfyUI (the core nodes merged 2026-11-10 and the templates want 0.45.0+), pull the four files into diffusion_models / text_encoders / vae, open the built-in MiniMax-H3-Image: Text to Image template, start at 4 MP on purpose so smaller cards do not choke, and raise the resolution when the GPU has room. Close on the honest boundary: the license gates companies over 1 Million USD revenue, the prompt expander is an extra 7.34 GB download switched off by default, and the VRAM floor is not officially stated anywhere.

claims.claim: MiniMax released H3-Image as an open-weight model for download, in one checkpoint covering both text-to-image and image editing.
The diffusion transformer is 33.1B parameters, distilled to a 6-step sampler with no classifier-free guidance.
The Comfy-Org repack needs exactly four files totalling 54.79 GB (21 GB + 25.28 GB + 7.34 GB + 1.17 GB) placed in three folders under ComfyUI/models.
The Comfy-Org repository published the repackage on 2026-11-08 and logged 351,803 downloads in its first month, versus 142,989 on MiniMax's own repo.
Native support merged into ComfyUI core on 2026-11-10 as feat: Support MiniMax-H3-image (CORE-708), and the docs templates require ComfyUI 0.45.0+ and template pack 0.11.104+.
The text-to-image template deliberately opens at 4 MP, below the model's native 16 MP, so low-VRAM machines do not run out of memory.
The BF16 checkpoint is 68.65 GB and its required text encoder another 66.7 GB, which is why the INT8 repack exists.
The license requires separate written authorization from MiniMax if your annualized revenue exceeds 1 Million USD or you provide hosted services to third parties.
MiniMax's announcement claims a 4K (4096 x 4096) image in under 10 seconds, at up to 5x the speed of mainstream alternatives.
claims.source_title: Bringing 4K Image Generation into the 10-Second Era

claims.claim: A third-party quantized variant (PrunaAI P-H3-Image) lists From 21 GB of VRAM peaking at 8 MP, against 143 GB of weights for MiniMax-H3; it is a modified model, not the Comfy-Org path.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: Downloading a game and its HD texture pack, not installing a mod
analogy_candidates.mapping: The model is a AAA game engine; Comfy-Org's INT8 files are the official compressed download; the four files land in named folders exactly like a game's /models directories; ComfyUI itself is the launcher that must be updated first.
analogy_candidates.limit: the viewer starts imagining paid DLC or always-online checks -- everything here is free and offline once downloaded; the only gate is a license clause for million-dollar companies.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: A studio camera that shoots 16 MP in one shot versus a phone app that upscales a 1 MP snapshot
analogy_candidates.mapping: H3-Image renders native 16 MP in a single pass, where most local models output 1-4 MP and get upscaled afterwards.
analogy_candidates.limit: the viewer expects photography physics like lenses and exposure -- generation has no optics, and 16 MP costs real compute per image, not just a bigger sensor.

misconceptions.myth: You need to install a custom node pack from some third party to run MiniMax H3-Image in ComfyUI.
misconceptions.reality: Support merged into ComfyUI core on 2026-11-10 (feat: Support MiniMax-H3-image (CORE-708)), and the Comfy-Org docs point at built-in template workflows; update ComfyUI instead of hunting custom nodes. (claim 5)

misconceptions.myth: The download is one model file.
misconceptions.reality: Four files go into three different folders (diffusion model 21 GB, text encoder 25.28 GB, optional prompt expander 7.34 GB, VAE 1.17 GB), and the expander is optional. (claim 3)

misconceptions.myth: The famous runs-on-an-RTX-3060 / 42.5 GB claims apply to H3-Image.
misconceptions.reality: Those numbers come from Comfy-Org's August day-0 blog about the MiniMax H3 video model's memory optimization (from 123.6 GB in full precision to 42.5 GB), not the image model; no official H3-Image VRAM floor exists. (claim 10, Unverified)

glossary.definition: The numbered files that make a model work are published for anyone to download and run on their own machine, not just through the company's website.
The website where AI models are hosted for download, like an app store for model files.
The model file itself; the trained weights that turn text into images.
The image-generating core of the system; it refines a field of static noise into a picture step by step.
The model part that reads your prompt first and turns it into numbers the image generator understands.
The decoder that translates the model's internal compressed image into the actual PNG you can open.
A free, node-based app for running image and video models locally, where you wire boxes together instead of typing into a single box.
A shrink-wrapped version of the model that stores numbers more roughly (8-bit instead of 16-bit) so it fits in less memory, at a small quality cost.
The memory sitting on your graphics card; models must fit inside it to run fast.
How many denoising passes the model takes; H3-Image is fixed at 6, which is few.
A common second pass that checks the image against your prompt; H3-Image skips it (guidance fixed at 1), so there is no negative prompt.
A measure of image size; 16 MP is roughly a 4096 x 4096 canvas, several times the pixel count of a typical 1080p wallpaper.
An optional small language model that rewrites your short prompt into the detailed paragraph the image model reads best.
A ready-made wiring diagram that ships inside ComfyUI; you open it and press run instead of building the graph yourself.
A free-to-use license with conditions; here, companies above 1 Million USD a year must ask MiniMax for written permission.

unverified: No official minimum VRAM or system-RAM requirement for MiniMax-H3-Image has been published by MiniMax or Comfy-Org; any specific GB floor for running it locally is community folklore until measured or stated.
Community posts report H3-family models running on cards as small as 8-12 GB with heavy quantization, but none of those numbers are confirmed by a tier 1-3 page for H3-Image specifically.
The under 10 seconds 4K generation time is MiniMax's own API-side claim with no published hardware or method; local speed on a viewer's GPU is unknown and will differ.

Whether the just-merged core support (2026-11-10) has shipped in a stable ComfyUI release, or only in nightly builds, is not stated on any fetched page; the docs warn template nodes may lag stable releases.
Reddit and X reception threads (r/LocalLLaMA, r/comfyui) could not be fetched this run (403 blocks), so community sentiment is ungrounded.
suggested_outline:
Hook: three days ago this model did not exist outside MiniMax's servers; last night ComfyUI itself learned to run it -- and the Comfy-Org download page already shows 351,803 pulls.
Name what the viewer has: a gaming PC with a decent GPU and ComfyUI curiosity; this is the first open-weight image model that natively shoots about 16 MP in 6 steps.
Explain the three cooperating parts with the game-install analogy: ComfyUI is the launcher (update it first, core support merged 2026-11-10), the four files are the game (21 GB DiT + 25.28 GB text encoder + 7.34 GB expander + 1.17 GB VAE into three named folders), the template is the saved game (open and run).
The payoff run: open the built-in Text to Image template, notice it starts at 4 MP on purpose, write a prompt, raise resolution when the GPU has room.
Honest catch: no official VRAM floor exists, the RTX 3060 stories are about the H3 video model, and the license gates million-dollar companies -- measure on your own card before promising viewers a number.
notes: Conflicts and thin spots. The RTX 3060 / 42.5 GB / 66% memory-reduction claims in the Comfy day-0 blog (blog.comfy.org) describe the MiniMax H3 video model launched in August, not H3-Image; do not attribute them to the image model on screen. The 21 GB VRAM peak figure belongs to PrunaAI's modified P-H3-Image quant (8 steps, 8 MP, up to 8 references), not the Comfy-Org INT8 path this video teaches; kept as claim 10 with that framing. Downloads on the two HF repos will keep moving after this run; the quoted 351,803 and 142,989 are the values printed on the pages fetched 2026-11-11 and MiniMax's own blog says weights were released with the announcement. Kingy.ai's file sizes cover the H3 video files, not H3-Image; its value here is the explicit statement that no minimum-VRAM matrix has been published. The HN item URL given as a seed returned an empty body this run; the Algolia API search confirms an H3-Image story posted 2026-11-10 at 4 points with 0 comments, which matches the radar seed. Reddit and X reception threads were blocked (403) and are ungrounded.
viewer_situation: You have a gaming PC or Mac with a decent GPU, you have used ChatGPT to make pictures, and you have heard people run image models themselves in ComfyUI but never tried a brand-new one this early.
process_steps: Update ComfyUI to the latest version (0.45.0+; core MiniMax-H3-Image support merged 2026-11-10).
Download the four files from the Comfy-Org Hugging Face repos: the 21 GB INT8 diffusion model, the 25.28 GB INT8 text encoder, the 7.34 GB prompt expander, and the 1.17 GB VAE.
Place them in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models, ComfyUI/models/text_encoders (two files), and ComfyUI/models/vae.
Open the built-in MiniMax-H3-Image: Text to Image template from the workflow template library.
Run once at the template's default 4 MP canvas, then raise resolution with the selector when the GPU has headroom.
objection: A skeptical engineer says the four-file package is still 54.79 GB, no official VRAM floor is published, the merged core support is hours old, and a 12 GB card may simply choke on a 33.1B-parameter DiT no matter how good the INT8 repack is.
